long_biography.plain_text:
Optasia's mobile-credit platform shows how Bassim Haidar turned telecommunications infrastructure into financial technology. The system uses data from network operators to score borrowers, distribute small advances and collect repayments in emerging markets. Its development built on his earlier experience supplying radio links, telecom equipment and logistics services to African operators.

Haidar was born in Nigeria to Lebanese parents and studied at Beirut University College. He returned to Nigeria at 20 and co-founded his first communications business, then developed procurement and infrastructure companies as mobile networks expanded. After leading Optasia from its foundation through 2021, he moved into a non-executive board role, retaining a connection to the financial-technology company he created.
